BIGFOOT by CyberLight Game Studio is a survival horror game centered around one of the most famous legends in North American folklore: the mysterious creature known as Bigfoot, also called Sasquatch. The game originally entered Early Access in January 2017 and has continued receiving updates and redesigns over time. Players can either become hunters attempting to track and kill the creature or play as the monster itself in multiplayer matches.

Below is an extensive overview.

BIGFOOT exists in a category of horror games that does not rely entirely on scripted jump scares or cinematic moments. Instead, the experience builds tension through uncertainty. Many horror games immediately reveal the danger to the player, but BIGFOOT approaches fear differently. It creates an atmosphere where players know something dangerous exists in the forest, but they do not always know where it is, how close it may be, or whether the sounds around them are genuine threats.

The forests in BIGFOOT feel isolated. Trees block visibility. Mountains interrupt movement. Fog sometimes limits awareness. During daytime, players may feel relatively safe while collecting supplies and exploring the environment. Night changes everything. Darkness transforms familiar areas into dangerous spaces where every noise suddenly becomes important.

The basic premise sounds simple: find Bigfoot and eliminate him. However, the game quickly demonstrates that the objective is more complicated than it appears.

As a hunter, the player enters large wilderness areas and begins searching for evidence. Supplies are scattered around the map. Weapons and tools become necessary for survival. Cameras can be placed around forests to detect movement. Traps can injure or slow Bigfoot. Medical kits help recover health after attacks.

Players are not simply running toward a target marker. They are investigating an environment.

The process often becomes:

Search for clues.

Locate signs of Bigfoot activity.

Set traps.

Monitor camera footage.

Stay alive.

Adapt when the plan fails.

This structure creates a rhythm unlike traditional shooters. Long periods of preparation can suddenly explode into chaos within seconds.

Imagine a multiplayer session with four hunters.

At the beginning, everyone feels confident.

Someone finds extra ammunition.

Someone else places cameras.

One player insists they heard footsteps.

Nobody believes them.

Ten minutes later, one teammate disappears into the darkness.

Screaming starts through voice chat.

A massive creature suddenly emerges from the trees and attacks.

The organized strategy immediately turns into panic.

Moments like this are largely responsible for BIGFOOT becoming popular among groups of friends and content creators.

The multiplayer component dramatically changes the experience because human behavior itself creates entertainment.

Players often separate from the group even when they should not.

Players accidentally trigger traps.

Players waste ammunition.

Players become convinced they saw movement.

Players argue over directions.

Players forget where vehicles are parked.

Then Bigfoot appears.

The result is usually confusion and chaos.

The game supports hunter teams against AI Bigfoot and also player-controlled Bigfoot matches, where one player assumes the role of the creature itself.

Playing as Bigfoot completely changes the perspective of the game.

Instead of being the hunted, the player becomes the predator.

As Bigfoot, direct attacks are not always the best approach.

Patience becomes important.

Hunters frequently expect immediate combat, but Bigfoot performs best through pressure and psychological manipulation.

Bigfoot can:

Hide in darkness.

Observe hunters.

Attack unexpectedly.

Set ambushes.

Retreat and recover.

Use speed and strength advantages.

The interesting aspect is that Bigfoot does not necessarily behave like a giant monster running directly toward enemies.

The creature often behaves like a predator.

Predators do not always attack immediately.

Predators watch.

Predators wait.

Predators choose moments carefully.

This design creates tension because players begin questioning every sound.

A branch breaking in the distance becomes suspicious.

A camera suddenly disconnecting becomes suspicious.

Movement between trees becomes suspicious.

Even silence becomes suspicious.

One of the strongest aspects of BIGFOOT is environmental design.

The maps contain forests, caves, rivers, lakes, mountains, campsites, abandoned locations, and wilderness areas intended to feel enormous and isolated. The environments are designed so players can never fully see everything around them.

Large open spaces would reduce fear because players could see approaching danger.

Dense forests do the opposite.

Trees create uncertainty.

Darkness creates uncertainty.

Distance creates uncertainty.

Uncertainty creates tension.

The sound design plays a major role as well.

Many players discover that BIGFOOT becomes much scarier with headphones.

You hear:

Wind moving through trees.

Footsteps.

Animal noises.

Branches snapping.

Roars in the distance.

Sudden impacts against cabins.

Heavy breathing.

Because the game relies heavily on audio information, players become increasingly sensitive to sound.

A distant noise can cause an entire group to stop moving.

Someone usually asks:

"Did you hear that?"

Then everyone becomes quiet.

Nothing happens.

Five seconds later chaos begins.

The game also creates stories that players remember after finishing sessions.

Unlike scripted games where everyone experiences identical events, BIGFOOT produces situations naturally.

A player may accidentally step into their own trap.

Someone may run out of ammunition during an attack.

Someone may become separated from the team and spend twenty minutes hiding.

Someone may sacrifice themselves so teammates can survive.

These moments become personal stories.

Many multiplayer games create matches.

BIGFOOT often creates memories.

The title also evolved significantly during its life cycle. Since entering Early Access, the game has received major redesigns and content updates over multiple versions.

Community reactions generally describe BIGFOOT as especially enjoyable with friends. Some players mention that it becomes less engaging after many hours, while others continue playing because of the unpredictable nature of multiplayer sessions and updates. Community discussions frequently focus on funny moments, bugs, tension, and memorable hunts.

Part of BIGFOOT's appeal comes from the idea that nobody ever feels entirely comfortable.

If players stay together, resources become limited.

If players separate, they become vulnerable.

If players hide, they lose information.

If players attack aggressively, they risk death.

Every decision contains tradeoffs.

That constant balancing act keeps players uncertain.

BIGFOOT ultimately succeeds because it transforms a simple mythological creature into a survival experience based on atmosphere, cooperation, and fear of the unknown. Rather than presenting horror as a sequence of scripted events, it creates systems that allow tension to emerge naturally.

Players do not simply fight a monster.

They enter its territory.

And in BIGFOOT, the forest often feels like it belongs to the creature long before players arrive.

Игра оставила смешанные впечатления. Больше всего понравилась атмосфера — ночью в лесу реально становится напряжённо, особенно когда Бигфут внезапно нападает. Камеры, капканы и приманка с мясом добавляют интереса, первое время играть довольно весело и местами даже страшно.

Но минусов тоже хватает. Если понять, когда Бигфут атакует, убить его становится слишком легко, из-за чего пропадает весь страх. В игре с друзьями баланс вообще ломается — игрок за Бигфута может просто в начале матча быстро всех перебить. Также игра почти не обновляется, Бигфут часто застревает в текстурах, что сильно портит впечатление.

В целом игра подойдёт, чтобы пару часов посмеяться с друзьями и немного потрепать себе нервы, но контента и механик мало, поэтому быстро становится скучно. И да, несмотря на всё это, я каким-то образом наиграл 16 часов. Видимо, я просто ебнутый.
